newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to shut ineffective overseas outposts.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to shut ineffective overseas outposts.

text.p: Taiwan, which recently severed unofficial ties with Cambodia, plans to shut down several "ineffective" overseas representative offices, its state-funded news agency reported on Monday.
The Central News Agency quoted Foreign Minister John Chang as saying the ministry would close three to four unofficial offices abroad, including in Libya, as early as this week.
"There is no need for these unofficial outposts to continue their operations because they are ineffective in promoting ties," Chang was quoted as saying.
Chang did not name the other offices slated for closure.
The move came one week after Taipei recalled its representatives from Phnom Penh and ordered closure of Cambodia's Taipei office.

Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on July 22 ordered the closing of Taiwan's office, alleging that illicit Taiwanese aid was provided to the royalist forces of Co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh during fighting in early July.
Taipei has denied complicity in Cambodia's turmoil and laid the blame for the row squarely with communist China, saying Beijing was widening its diplomatic embargo of Taiwan to non-official spheres.
Beijing, rival of Taipei since a civil war split them in 1949, considers Taiwan a renegade province not entitled to foreign relations.
Chang said Taipei would not consider returning to Cambodia unless Phnom Penh acknowledged its mistake.
"We will only consider reopening Cambodia office unless Cambodia apologises," Chang told reporters.
Taiwan has diplomatic ties with only 30 countries -- mostly poor states dependent on the wealthy island for economic help.
It maintains unofficial relations with most other countries, including vibrant trade links with economic powers like the United States, Japan and even mainland China.
